body.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge 1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\); equivalently, the local profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At any law with a non-singleton identified set or without the separated-chart conditions, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks.
body.justification: Exact nuisance calibration preserves coverage at transitions, while the explicit Hausdorff comparison recovers ordinary Wald geometry on separated charts.
body.gap: Existing weak-identification and stable-bound procedures do not calibrate a profile discrepancy over this changing selected-SCM fiber or establish its first-order agreement with chart-specific Wald inference.
body.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty without interpreting a nonshrinking confidence fiber as point identification.

obligation.what_is_open: The uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact confidence-fiber inversion and the selected Wald ellipse for the globally defined atlas.
obligation.obstruction: Exact finite-sample coverage is independent of rank stability, but the Hausdorff assertion needs a uniform glued-chart likelihood expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.
obligation.attempted: Proved finite-sample Berger--Boos coverage from the preliminary-region event and exact super-uniform tail values, and reduced the local separated smooth case to the profile-Wald quadratic conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(q_0\) denote the true observable law and \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\). Exact inversion of each binomial tail and the stated Bonferroni allocation give
\[
P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)\le\beta_n.
\]
For fixed compatible \((q,t)\), define
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The upper-tail value is super-uniform, including at atoms: \(P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\) for \(u\in[0,1]\). Since \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\), on \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\) the supremum in \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) includes \(q_0\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\ge \min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\},
\]
and, because \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\),
\[
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
\le \beta_n+P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}
\le\alpha.
\]
This exact finite-sample argument is valid along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\). On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, the multinomial likelihood has the usual uniform quadratic expansion and the common incident Jacobian reduces the target profile to the Wald quadratic, yielding \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\to0\) in probability. The asserted global Hausdorff conclusion still requires proof that no nearby mixed-support component has been omitted and a uniform glued-chart profile expansion.
